author: Doctor
text:
A reminder to those of you looking at the eur/usd pair.

The daily chart of this pair gives us some hints of what may come to pass. The green lines are support and resistance marked off with an S and R as you will come to expect from my charts. I have a small box drawn in an area where we want to see a close above, the box is in a critical decision area. The 'A' shows the upper portion of the box and support/resistance being tested and a daily/weekly close with profit taking and an unwillingness to take it higher just yet.

The following last three candles 'B' all closed above the lower green line which is early signs of support coming in. It is still far too early to know if this will hold especially with no New York trading session today and the after London price action is effectively invalid for signals. Only automated trades are the likely orders flowing there.

Finally look at the 'C' area, there are buyers here that have all but been ignored when this price area was last tested and the move went nowhere. Closing above the box/upper green line will bring us into those buyers and also take out many longer term bearish stops and trigger new longs. Given we have come off low price levels going way back the pro money will be looking for new orders. Let price action be your guide.

author: Doctor
text:
Buckwalter, if you look closely at the price chop you mentioned you will see it consumed buyers as price wound up, but its goal was to reach the nearest sellers where it failed, note the price reaction down, very weak bearish candles, no strength or conviction in that market. It tried again and only got the sellers from a newer move up. Ask one question, if everyone is short the euro how come price didnt reach willing sellers?.....and why did the following move down not continue?

The answer is on the monthly chart, we hit lows from way back and pro money knows this is a good place to buy. Both pro money and price have very long memories, retail traders have neither. If you have a few billion to trade longer time frames, would you sell now?.....who would you be selling from and who would buy the position back from you when you want profit?

The decision area I highlighted is the real test of euro selling, what was selling can become buying as resistance can become support and as supply and become demand. This plus a bullish looking candle meaning the market is bearish and vice versa is what confuses many people. That decision area plus old buyers even though the market was bearish still mean buyers. Trend traders will no longer see a bearish trend in the euro, the major funds are likely gone long too and the dollar shorting will aid the euro for long positions.

If price were to fail in the decision area we have willing buyers at around the 1.23650 area and try pushing again from that level. Pro money will only run with it when they have enough orders in the market and when it comes off a sensible price level and with room for profit.

We again sit and wait to see where this will go, far to early to take a trade in any direction in eur/usd.

Nosbigs, they can patch their wounds with their worthless tickets on the floor:)

Mel, here is a chart for you. This is eur/usd on the 5min showing my short entry. It is taken off a reaction to an old decision area and an S/R area. My entry is on the close of the green candle I marked for you. Target is very close now and may be hit by the time I type this and post it. NY open is 1.5 hours away and any shorts need to exercise caution and not be too greedy.

There is lots of short term profit tied up in the bullish moves over the past two weeks and some of this has to be taken out of the market. Take little bites where there is room for profit and watch for developing support and resistance.

author: Doctor
text:
doubleFF, IF and I were discussing it live as it happened between us and not on here. We were also discussing serious world affairs such as womens butt's, surfing and holiday's. Tough session!

Simon, I am looking for your charts now. The 1hr you have looks about right, the selling came in on the last green candle. Its not possible to align the times as we both seem to have different time zones. If price leaves your area of interest fast, you have two options, be in at the break and pull back on a low time frame, or wait for price to retrace on a higher time frame and take a entry then when the original break area supply is tested. Break outs are not something that inspire me, most do not work out. Taking a test is much safer.

There was a time when I used Bollinger bands and the CCI, but they like all other indicators distract your eye from where it should be i.e looking at price only. Try an experiment, remove the bollinger bands for a week and only look at the 15min and higher time frames. See can your eye and brain spot what to most people is obvious in hindsight, the skill is in seeing the areas I mention in real time and on low time frames. You appear to be developing a good eye and I like how you also mention the 4hr in your chart, good stuff and valuable you stick with this approach. Stay with it.

Scaling into a position is ok once you dont have too many orders to close and be sure to cancel others that are still waiting. Never enter while the market is at terminal velocity.
